You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testAddNonComparable()` is designed to verify that adding a plain `Object` to an instance of `Frequency` should throw an IllegalArgumentException. The current implementation of `Frequency.addValue(Object v)` (lines 108-111) simply casts the `Object` to `Comparable<?>` and calls `addValue(Comparable<?>)`. This means it accepts any Object at the call site but actually expects it to be Comparable at runtime. If this cast fails or the subsequent use fails due to non-comparable objects, exceptions will occur.

The method `addValue(Comparable<?> v)` (lines 123-139) tries to add the given Comparable to a frequency table (likely a TreeMap) which requires keys to be comparable. If the value is not compatible with the existing keys, the TreeMap operations throw a `ClassCastException`, which is caught and wrapped as an `IllegalArgumentException` with the message "Value not comparable to existing values."

The issue is that the first call to `addValue(Object)` does not explicitly check if the passed object indeed implements Comparable. The cast happens unchecked, so a plain Object passes through, but then internally when adding to the TreeMap, it fails if the object doesn't implement Comparable or is not comparable with existing keys. Thus, the first addition of a plain Object is incorrectly allowed but causes failure on subsequent additions.

In summary, the root cause of the failure is that `addValue(Object)` casts to `Comparable` without checking compatibility before passing the value to `addValue(Comparable<?>)`. This permits non-comparable objects to be added initially but breaks the frequency map later, which is why the test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` on the first addition itself, but the current code does not throw it until later.

This diagnosis aligns with the current bug report's description stating that `addValue(Object)` should not accept plain `Object` values but only Comparable ones. The test tries to verify this behavior expecting an immediate exception which is not currently thrown.

The recent bug reports retrieved are irrelevant to this issue.

Next, I can suggest appropriate fixes likely involving adding a proper `instanceof Comparable` check in `addValue(Object)` before casting and allowing addition.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testAddNonComparable()` attempts to add a plain `Object` (which is not Comparable) to a `Frequency` instance and expects an `IllegalArgumentException`. The implementation of `Frequency.addValue(Object)` simply casts the input to `Comparable<?>` without verifying if it actually implements Comparable. This unchecked cast allows a non-Comparable object to pass through initially. Inside `addValue(Comparable<?>)`, a TreeMap is used to track frequencies, relying on values being Comparable for key ordering. If a non-Comparable is added, TreeMap operations throw a `ClassCastException`, caught and re-thrown as an `IllegalArgumentException` during subsequent additions. Thus, the first addition of a plain Object is incorrectly allowed, whereas an exception is expected immediately. The bug report explains this mismatch, noting the API should reject non-Comparable objects upfront. The root cause is the missing type check in `addValue(Object)`. Recent bug reports are unrelated to this issue.

Suggested fix involves adding an explicit `instanceof Comparable` check in `addValue(Object)` before casting and adding values.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
